acceptanceCriteria: Each spec governing affected ranges, CEM base/head ranges and Tasks claim bases states whether it assumes a first-parent/trunk-based history.

Each states the observed behaviour (refusal code or uncertainty) when base is not an ancestor of head or the range crosses a non-first-parent merge, cited to a test or recorded observation; unverified cases stay NOT_OBSERVED.
body: Idea source: Anthropic engineering post 'Redesigning source control' (anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control), reviewed 2026-10-16. Idea only; no text copied. Scion stores each changeset relative to its first parent and states that this assumes trunk-based development. Corvint makes the same assumption implicitly: `corvint affected --base`, CEM base..head ranges, AFP qualification counting first-parent commits on main (V1-0039), and the Tasks recovery that re-claims at `merge^1` after a merged-forward branch. None of the governing specs states the assumption or what happens on a non-linear base (octopus merge, merge from a side branch, base not an ancestor of head). Idea: one sentence-level statement in each governing spec plus the documented refusal or uncertainty when the assumption fails.
title: docs: state the first-parent / trunk-based history assumption behind affected --base, CEM ranges and Tasks re-claim at merge^1
